name: SMC Wing, N83/N84 field 14 (Hubble)
blurb: N83/N84 field 14, a star field in the wing of the Small Magellanic Cloud, seen by Hubble.
label: n83f14wfc-hubble
story: A crowd of stars in the wing of the Small Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf galaxy and satellite of the Milky Way, near the star-forming regions N83 and N84. Hubble charted these stars to find how far away the surrounding gas clouds lie, building a three-dimensional map of the gas in this tidally disrupted wing, whose distance helps trace the Small Cloud's past collision with the Large Magellanic Cloud.

claims.text: N83-F14-WFC is one of the ACS/WFC pointings of program 17509 covering the N83/N84 star-forming regions
N83 and N84 are star-forming regions in the wing of the Small Magellanic Cloud
The Small Magellanic Cloud is a dwarf galaxy
The Small Magellanic Cloud is a satellite of the Milky Way
The program uses stars to measure distances to the gas and map the region's 3D gas structure
The wing is tidally disrupted, and its distance constrains the SMC-LMC collision history
